cards.explanation: The answer is the thickets of Arabia, friends. Isaiah says it plain: "In the thickets of Arabia you must lodge, O caravans of Dedanites." (Isaiah 21:13) The Dedanites are traveling people, and this is where they have to stay. I think a thicket makes a pretty scratchy hotel.

The answer is water, friends. Isaiah says, "Bring water for the thirsty, O dwellers of Tema…" (Isaiah 21:14). Tema is a place in Arabia, and its people are the ones he's calling out to. A cold cup of water for someone in need is a simple thing to hand over.

The answer is True! Right after the water, Isaiah says, "meet the refugees with food." (Isaiah 21:14). So Tema is told to bring both drink and food. The next verse says these refugees flee from the sword, the bow and the stress of battle (Isaiah 21:15).

The answer is the sword and the bow in battle, friends. Isaiah says they flee "…from the sword—the sword that is drawn—from the bow that is bent, and from the stress of battle." (Isaiah 21:15). Swords and bows are the weapons right there in the verse. These folks ran from a fight, and that's why they need help.

The answer is that it will all be gone, friends. The Lord says to Isaiah, "Within one year, as a hired worker would count it, all the glory of Kedar will be gone." (Isaiah 21:16) Kedar is a people of Arabia. A hired worker counts the time carefully, so it's a set year. All of it, not just some.
The answer is False. The Lord says, "The remaining archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few." (Isaiah 21:17) Few is the word, not many. The archers of Kedar don't come out ahead here.

The answer is Israel, friends. Isaiah closes with "For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken." (Isaiah 21:17) That's how the message ends, with the One who spoke it. Everything before it carries that weight.
